title: check: one bad historical blob aborts check; sync writes no revocations
description:
One unreadable historical version of any registry path aborts check entirely: export, sync, query, keys and status all fail. Sync then writes no revocation file, and because sync refuses a rewind, the registry cannot recover.

Where (HEAD 4237c43): read_blobs at git-vouch:246-251, file_history at 320-321 and registry_history at 1279-1280 raise VouchError for a historical blob over 64 KiB or a non-regular mode (symlink, submodule). check_registry (1429) lets it propagate. cmd_sync calls check_registry at 2388, before the revocation write at 2391.

Reproduced (scratchpad a1/big.sh): commit a 70,000-byte revocations/zz-1.json, delete it in the next commit, then commit a valid revocation of alice's key. check prints "revocations/zz-1.json: a version is not a blob of at most 65536 bytes" and exits 1, with no tiers. export writes nothing, not even the revocation file.

Why it matters: DESIGN.md says "sync writes the revocation file even when check fails on something else, so a revocation always spreads." Once such a commit is merged (a merger who ignored check, or a later git-vouch that tightens a cap), every user's sync fails forever. New revocations never reach anyone, and the only repair is a history rewrite that `_fetch` refuses by design. A malformed working-tree file, by contrast, is just a problem.

Fix: treat an unreadable historical version like an unparsable one. Record it as content that is present but unreadable (record_at already maps unparsable bytes to None), add a problem naming path and commit, and carry on, so the revocation file is still computed and written. Keep failing closed for allowed_signers through `problems`.
